pool.text: The city received its present name of Khabarovsk after being previously known as Khabarovka.
A department of the Russian Geographical Society formed to establish libraries, theatres and museums.
The Khabarovsk Bridge across the Amur was completed, allowing Trans-Siberian trains to cross.
Khabarovsk was occupied by Japan during the Russian Civil War in September.
The Directorate of Road Construction of Eastern Siberia and the Far East was created.
The city of Khabarovsk was divided into two districts named Stalinsky and Kirovsky.
The Tsentralny district of Khabarovsk was formed by the Far Eastern Executive Committee.
The Zheleznodorozhny District was created in the city of Khabarovsk.
The Krasnoflotsky District of Khabarovsk was created on September fifteenth.
The first phase of the city tram system was commissioned in Khabarovsk.
The Khabarovsk television studio officially began broadcasting in the city.
The Stalinsky District of Khabarovsk was officially renamed to Industrialny.
Niigata in Japan became twinned with the city of Khabarovsk.
The Khabarovsk Institute of Physical Education opened its doors on September first.
Khabarovsk was awarded the Order of October Revolution on January fourteenth.
The first stage of the urban trolley system opened in Khabarovsk.
The Bandy World Championship tournament was played in the city.
Portland in the United States established a twinning relationship with Khabarovsk.
Victoria in Canada became twinned with the city of Khabarovsk.
Khabarovsk successfully held its very first mayoral elections.
